newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Thiessen says economy to sustain growth.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Thiessen says economy to sustain growth.

text.p: Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen said on Wednesday that Canada had laid the groundwork for sustained economic growth after a difficult period of restructuring.

"We are now in better shape than we have been in years to face the economic challenges of the future," Thiessen told a Quebec business group. He said that restructuring in Canada had acted as a drag on output and employment in the past.
"But I believe we are now at the stage where the payoffs from these necessary adjustments have begun to outweigh the difficulties," he said.
Thiessen said there was still a wide margin of spare production capacity or output gap in the economy.
"There is room for strong growth in coming quarters without too much concern about a flare-up in inflation."
But he continued, "As slack in the economy is taken up, we won't need as much monetary stimulus as we have now to keep the economy on a sustainable low inflation growth path."
Thiessen said he was very encouraged by the performance of the interest-rate sensitive sectors of the economy.
He pointed to significant increases in spending on houses, motor vehicles and consumer durables.
He also said growth in private sector employment had resumed.
Thiessen repeated that the bank remained committed to keeping inflation within a target band of 1 to 3 percent.
"It is only by maintaining Canada's low rate of inflation that monetary policy will help to consolidate a durable economic expansion," he said.
But he said the bank did not have the tools to fine-tune the Canadian economy.
"It takes considerable time -- one to two years -- for monetary policy actions to have an effect on the economy," he said.
